name: Somerset Road Dispersed Camping Area - Green Mountain National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Manchester Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general forest dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout national forest lands along Forest Road 71 (Somerset Road). Must be set back 200 feet from roads, trails, and water bodies.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6-8 inches deep in forest topsoil, 200 feet from Deerfield River and Somerset Reservoir. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Black bears present: bear canister or vehicle storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only within forest.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Vermont FPR burn danger warnings.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state route changing to unpaved gravel forest road (Somerset Road / FS 71)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel forest road with frost heaves and mud spots during spring thaw.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main Somerset gravel road in dry summer/fall conditions)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE on open ridge points; weak down near river reservoir
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Green Mountain ridges restrict cell line of sight)

amenities: Glacial River & Reservoir Water Access (Filter required)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: May thaw ('Mud Season'): cold (40-55°F), high snowmelt mud, road gates opening around late May.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 70-80°F, ideal Vermont mountain summer, cool comfortable nights (50-55°F).
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: World-famous Vermont maple autumn foliage (50-65°F daytime, 25-35°F nights), prime camping.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe mountain winter (10-25°F), heavy snowpack, Somerset Road unplowed (groomed snowmobile trail).

dangers_and_hazards: Black Bears active in Green Mountains - bear-proof food storage mandatory
Moose collision hazard on Somerset Road
Spring mud traps on unpaved roads

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional camper vehicle on Somerset Road

common_plants_and_trees: Sugar Maple (Acer saccharum - Vermont State Tree)

human_demographics_and_culture: Vermont Long Trail backpackers, mountain bikers, fly anglers, digital nomads, and autumn maple leaf peepers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Abnaki and Mahican indigenous traditions revere the Green Mountains ('Ndakinna' - Our Land) as sacred ancestral spirit mountains.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Sugar maple forest aroma and energy, pristine mountain stream acoustics, peaceful Vermont sanctuary.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding mountain trail through maple forest and high ridge vistas

public_reviews_summary: Spectacular free primitive camping in the Green Mountains of Southern Vermont. Peaceful maple forests, pristine rivers, and solid cell service on high turnouts.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. Abundant firewood.
